verdicts.quote: “Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth)”
verdicts.reason: Vendor authorization docs specify OAuth2 with token exchange and scopes. ([docs.ramp.com](https://docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/authorization.txt))

verdicts.quote: “Publishing an app for other Ramp businesses takes two approvals: a partner application… and a production access application for your app…”
verdicts.reason: Public, multi‑tenant apps require acceptance into the partner program before production access; that’s partner_gated rather than merely app_review. ([support.ramp.com](https://support.ramp.com/accessing-the-developer-api/))

verdicts.quote: “use the Developer API… [for] the full Ramp data model.”
verdicts.reason: Official docs and OpenAPI indicate many resources (e.g., transactions, cards, bills, users, reimbursements, vendors), consistent with a broad API. ([docs.ramp.com](https://docs.ramp.com/llms.txt))

verdicts.quote: “Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account.”
verdicts.reason: Hosted at mcp.ramp.com and documented by Ramp, indicating an official MCP server. ([docs.ramp.com](https://docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/ramp-mcp.txt))

verdicts.quote: “Publishing an app for other Ramp businesses takes two approvals: a partner application… and a production access application…”
verdicts.reason: A Composio-style multi‑tenant toolkit would need partner-program approval before production OAuth, so outreach is required. ([support.ramp.com](https://support.ramp.com/accessing-the-developer-api/))
